gen-eater-gf-noto-naskh-arabic: Dark and jagged up top, then surprisingly refined below. Eater snarls in display weight while Noto Naskh Arabic stands tall and lightly engraved; try the heading big.
gen-eater-gf-noto-nastaliq-urdu: Eater comes in dark and aggressive, its thin strokes spaced wide apart over sturdier stems. Noto Nastaliq Urdu is the text serif beneath, dignified and tightly stacked.
gen-eater-gf-noto-rashi-hebrew: Noto Rashi Hebrew reads bookish and classic, with stubby ascenders. Above it, Eater adds a menacing, widely spaced snarl, so the page feels like a dusty tome with a threat stamped on its cover.
gen-eater-gf-noto-serif-ahom: Noto Serif Ahom reads traditional and dignified, lofty in its lowercase, with joins that thin gently but never vanish. Eater sits over it as the dark, wide-spaced troublemaker, and the stately body keeps its menace in check.
gen-eater-gf-noto-serif-armenian: Noto Serif Armenian brings big open counters and a mild, approachable stroke contrast, giving it an authoritative, traditional voice. And Eater, dark and wide-spaced on top, makes that steadiness feel even more welcome as the text unfolds.
gen-eater-gf-noto-serif-balinese: Noto Serif Balinese gives lowercase letters real vertical presence, with strokes sitting between flat and dramatic. Noto Serif Balinese then carries a long stretch of text like an editorial column, traditional and easy on the eye, while Eater growls above.
gen-eater-gf-noto-serif-bengali: Menacing meets polished here. Noto Serif Bengali settles into a dense, refined band of text with trimmed ascenders and slightly thinner hairlines, while Eater snarls above it.
gen-eater-gf-noto-serif-devanagari: Eater is dark and aggressive, with wide gaps between thin strokes and sturdy stems. Noto Serif Devanagari answers with a literary, classic body, short in its ascenders and big in its lowercase, which is the pair's sharpest quality.
gen-eater-gf-noto-serif-dogra: Eater looks dark and aggressive, its thin strokes and heavier stems spaced far apart. Noto Serif Dogra follows as a bookish text serif, with capitals barely taller than lowercase and a faint crayon-like rhythm that makes paragraphs feel handmade.
gen-eater-gf-noto-serif-ethiopic: Noto Serif Ethiopic reads bookish and classic, its words forming solid blocks rather than jagged skylines. Eater earns its keep big and short, where its dark, aggressive, widely spaced letters can bite.
